topics.syllabus: Basic control system components; Feedback principle; Transfer function; Block diagram representation; Signal flow graph.

cards.title: Closed loop and what feedback buys you
cards.titleHtml: Closed loop and what feedback buys you
cards.bodyHtml: For a forward path GGG with feedback HHH, negative feedback divides the open-loop gain by 1+GH1+GH1+GH. The same factor divides the sensitivity of the closed-loop gain to drift in GGG, which is the real reason feedback is used: gain is cheap, gain accuracy is not.
cards.pitfallHtml: SHT≈−1S^T_H\approx-1SHT​≈−1 is the whole design lesson: precision belongs in the feedback network, not in the amplifier.

cards.title: Mason's gain formula
cards.bodyHtml: Faster than block reduction whenever loops touch each other in awkward ways, and GATE asks it directly. Two loops are non-touching if they share no node and no branch.
cards.pitfallHtml: Signs: a loop gain already carries the −1-1−1 of its own summing junction, so a unity negative-feedback loop is L=−GHL=-GHL=−GH and Δ=1+GH\Delta=1+GHΔ=1+GH. Double-counting that minus is the usual slip.

cards.title: Block-diagram moves worth memorising
cards.bodyHtml: Only three rules are needed, and each is just 'keep every signal unchanged'. Moving a take-off point backwards past a block GGG requires a GGG in the new branch; moving it forwards requires 1/G1/G1/G. For a summing junction the rule is the mirror image.

cards.title: Steady-state error and system type
cards.bodyHtml: Type = number of poles at the origin in the open-loop G(s)H(s)G(s)H(s)G(s)H(s); order = degree of the denominator. They are different things and the question always means type. A type-NNN system tracks inputs up to tN−1t^{N-1}tN−1 with zero error and the tNt^{N}tN input with a finite error.
cards.pitfallHtml: These constants are defined for unity feedback. With H(s)≠1H(s)\neq1H(s)=1, either absorb HHH or work the error signal out from the actual diagram — the error being measured is R−CR-CR−C, not R−CHR-CHR−CH.

cards.title: Dominant poles and pole–zero cancellation
cards.bodyHtml: A pole five times further left than another contributes a term that has decayed to nothing before the slow one has moved, so the response is effectively second order. This is what lets the formulas above be applied to higher-order systems.

cards.title: Routh array, including the two special cases
cards.titleHtml: Routh array, including the two special cases
cards.bodyHtml: Necessary condition first: all coefficients present and of the same sign. If any is missing or of opposite sign the system is already unstable and no array is needed. Otherwise the number of sign changes in the first column equals the number of right-half-plane roots.
cards.pitfallHtml: A full row of zeros means roots on the jωj\omegajω axis or symmetric pairs — the system is marginally stable at best. Solving the auxiliary polynomial gives the exact jωj\omegajω-crossing frequency, which is often what the question actually wants.

zero in column 1 only⇒replace by ϵ→0+\text{zero in column 1 only}\Rightarrow\text{replace by }\epsilon\to0^{+}zero in column 1 only⇒replace by ϵ→0+
formulas.noteHtml: then continue and take limits

cards.title: Finding the range of K
cards.titleHtml: Finding the range of KKK
cards.bodyHtml: The standard question. Form 1+KG(s)H(s)=01+KG(s)H(s)=01+KG(s)H(s)=0, build the array with KKK symbolic, and force every first-column entry positive. The limiting KKK makes one entry zero — substitute it into the auxiliary equation to get the oscillation frequency.

cards.title: Root locus rules that decide answers
cards.bodyHtml: The locus is the set of sss where the angle condition holds; the gain condition only fixes which point corresponds to which KKK. Branches start at open-loop poles (K=0K=0K=0) and end at open-loop zeros or at infinity (K→∞K\to\inftyK→∞).
cards.pitfallHtml: Adding a zero pulls the locus left (more stable, faster); adding a pole pushes it right. If a question asks the effect of a compensator qualitatively, this is the answer.

topics.title: Bode, Nyquist, Margins and Compensation
topics.syllabus: Frequency response; Nyquist stability criterion; Bode plots; Lag, lead and lag-lead compensation.

cards.title: Bode plot by inspection
cards.bodyHtml: Write G(jω)G(j\omega)G(jω) in time-constant form. The low-frequency asymptote of a type-NNN system has slope −20N-20N−20N dB/dec and passes through ∣K∣|K|∣K∣ dB at ω=1\omega=1ω=1 (for N=0N=0N=0) or through 0 dB at ω=K1/N\omega=K^{1/N}ω=K1/N. Each pole then bends the slope by −20-20−20 dB/dec at its corner, each zero by +20+20+20.
cards.pitfallHtml: Type-1 systems: the initial −20-20−20 dB/dec line crosses 0 dB at ω=Kv\omega=K_vω=Kv​. Reading KvK_vKv​ straight off that intercept saves a page of algebra.

cards.title: Nyquist criterion
cards.bodyHtml: Count encirclements of the −1-1−1 point by the plot of G(jω)H(jω)G(j\omega)H(j\omega)G(jω)H(jω) as ω\omegaω runs from −∞-\infty−∞ to +∞+\infty+∞. Anticlockwise encirclements are counted positive.
cards.pitfallHtml: For an open-loop stable system (P=0P=0P=0) stability simply means the plot does not encircle −1-1−1. Only when GHGHGH itself has RHP poles do you need encirclements — and then a plot that misses −1-1−1 means the closed loop is unstable.

cards.title: Lead, lag and lag-lead
cards.bodyHtml: Lead adds phase near the crossover: faster response, more bandwidth, better transient — at the cost of amplifying noise. Lag adds gain at low frequency: better steady-state error, smaller bandwidth, slower. Lag-lead does both.
cards.pitfallHtml: A PD controller is lead-like (improves transient, raises ωgc\omega_{gc}ωgc​), a PI controller is lag-like and raises the system type by one, so it kills steady-state error. PID does both.

cards.title: State model and transfer function
cards.bodyHtml: The eigenvalues of AAA are the poles of the system, so stability can be read from AAA alone without ever forming the transfer function. The transfer function is unique; the state model is not — any similarity transform gives another valid one with the same eigenvalues.

cards.title: Controllability and observability
cards.bodyHtml: Both are rank tests. For an nnn-state system, full rank nnn means controllable (or observable); a rank deficiency means some mode cannot be driven by the input, or cannot be seen at the output.
cards.pitfallHtml: A pole–zero cancellation in G(s)G(s)G(s) is exactly a loss of controllability or observability — the cancelled mode is still there in the state model and can still be unstable.
